findings.body: The title and body describe only the `findings::summarise` helper, but the diff introduces a new kernel-bypass entrypoint, compose overlay, and configuration mounting. These changes are substantial and affect deployment. The PR description must list all changes; otherwise reviewers cannot assess the full scope.
findings.title: Describe all significant changes in the PR

findings.body: Repository rules require one `docs/modules/<module>/README.md` per src module. The new `summarise` module is added without a corresponding documentation file. Add `docs/modules/findings/summarise/README.md` describing the module's role and usage.
findings.title: Add README for the new summarise module

findings.body: When the truncated text contains no space, `head` is exactly `limit` characters, and appending the ellipsis produces a string of `limit + 1` characters, violating the documented "at most `limit` characters" contract. This could cause check-run titles to exceed GitHub's cap. Adjust the no-space branch to truncate to `limit - 1` before adding the ellipsis, or update the documentation to allow `limit + 1`.
findings.title: Ensure shorten never exceeds the stated limit

findings.body: The `globals_dict` variable is assigned but never used. The comment suggests it keeps `runpy` imported, but imports are not affected by variable assignment; the top-level `import runpy` already ensures the module is loaded. This line is dead code and should be removed for clarity.
findings.existing_code: globals_dict = runpy.run_path.__globals__  # noqa: F841 - keep runpy imported
findings.title: Remove redundant globals_dict assignment

value.summary: The pull request adds a `findings::summarise` helper but also contains significant deployment changes (kernel bypass, config mount, environment variables) not reflected in the description. The helper itself has a boundary bug where `shorten` can exceed its stated limit, and the new module lacks the required documentation README.
